root_idea.summary: The root denotes the removal or absence of one thing from another, leaving it bare, vacant, free, or unoccupied.
root_idea.development: From physical emptiness and freedom from occupation, the meanings extend to passing away, being alone or privately separated, leaving something free, and related states of release or detachment.

senses.definition: To pass away, go by, or be gone.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of earlier people, generations, events, or periods; the Quran also uses the form for what has gone before or passed out of the present situation.

senses.definition: To be alone with someone; to meet or converse in private.
senses.usage_conditions: Occurs with a person or group as the companion, including the Quranic construction خَلَوْا إِلَىٰ شَيَاطِينِهِمْ, “they were alone with their devils.”

senses.definition: To become available exclusively to someone; to be free for that person.
senses.usage_conditions: With لِـ, as in يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ, the construction expresses that a person or thing becomes exclusively available, bringing the relevant attention or favor to the beneficiary.

senses.definition: To release, let go, or leave free.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use; in فَخَلُّوا سَبِيلَهُمْ it means to leave their way free, hence to release them.

senses.definition: To become vacant or empty; to be left free of what occupied it.
senses.usage_conditions: An intransitive/reflexive use describing the subject as becoming cleared or emptied; the Quranic occurrence describes becoming empty.
Used adjectivally of times or generations that have already passed, as in الْأَيَّامِ الْخَالِيَةِ, “past days.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become empty, vacant, void, or devoid of occupants or contents.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a place, dwelling, vessel, thing, or the contents of the belly; this is a broader Classical use than the Quranic Form I senses listed above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become free from a fault, affair, or other thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with مِنْ or عَنْ, and also absolutely in the sense of being clear or free from an alleged fault or burden.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a woman, to be free from an obstacle to marriage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specific construction with عَنْ describing freedom from a legal or marital impediment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be alone with another in private seclusion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In a marital legal context, خَلْوَة may denote private seclusion with a spouse and has specified legal consequences before consummation; this technical qualification is Classical Arabic usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To devote oneself exclusively to religious service or exercises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The seclusion or withdrawal is understood as allowing the person to concentrate on worship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mock, ridicule, deride, or deceive someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative use of the private-occupation construction; the sources describe both ridicule and the related sense of attempting to deceive or outwit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rely on or depend upon someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction interpreted as betaking oneself to that person alone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat what is good, sweet, or pleasant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical use reported separately in the entry; it is not treated as a Quranic meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To confine oneself exclusively to an affair, a portion of food, or a selected she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of being alone in an affair or activity, restricting oneself to selected food, or confining oneself to a selected she-camel; this Form I exclusive-use construction is distinct from merely meeting someone in private.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave a place empty or vacant, or to make it so.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the idiomatic association of leaving one’s place vacant with dying; this causative emptying use is distinct from the Quranic command to release or leave free.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go one’s way, withdraw, or leave something or someone alone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of withdrawing from a person, affair, or place, and of leaving others free to act.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave, forsake, abandon, or part from someone; to become distant from him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form III construction is transitive with a person as its object and may emphasize separation or desertion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go out to someone in the field and confront him directly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use in which the parties meet in the open for direct engagement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wrestle or contend directly with another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The contest is undertaken one-on-one, without seeking assistance from others; the use may extend to contention in an affair or in war.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a place empty, or to find it empty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively of a place of dwelling or alighting; the two possibilities are respectively causing and discovering its vacancy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or find someone alone with oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction with a person as object and the speaker or another person as companion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go into an open or vacant tract to relieve oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily-function euphemism associated with going out into an unoccupied place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become vacant from occupation or business, or to confine oneself exclusively to an activity or object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes being at leisure, devoting oneself to an affair, and restricting one’s attention or consumption to selected food or a selected camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For camels, to be left to themselves without a herder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use describing animals left free to pasture without supervision.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask someone to leave his sitting-place vacant for the requester.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A request for the other person to vacate a particular seat or place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask for a private meeting or interview.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used when asking a king or another person to meet in a place unoccupied by others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Solitude, loneliness, or private seclusion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive denoting the state of being apart from others; it may also describe ease or privacy in conference.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An empty or unoccupied place, especially a private room or place of retreat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can denote the place in which a private meeting or retirement occurs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Either of the two sharp sides or edges of an arrowhead or spearhead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two edges together are called الخَلْوَتَانِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vacant place, open tract, or place containing nothing; specifically, a place used for relieving oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The substantive may denote an open or deserted area and, in a more specific use, a privy or place of bodily relief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Good or pleasant in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported in a phrase whose reading and assignment to this root are uncertain; the meaning is retained as a tentative Classical lexical item.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel released from restraint and left free to pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form is applied especially to a she-camel loosed from a binding of the forelimb and allowed to range freely.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A divorced woman, or a woman free from a husband or an obstacle to marriage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The marital sense is a metonymic extension of being left free; the word may be used as a divorce formula.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel selected or left for exclusive milking, including one made to accept and nourish another camel’s young.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical pastoral term covering several arrangements in which a camel is confined to the milking of the household or is made to yield milk through another young camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large ship, especially one that goes by itself or is accompanied by a small boat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized use distinct from the feminine adjective and camel term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A habitation or hive of bees in which honey is deposited.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May denote a manufactured hive, a hollow in wood or rock, or another container used by bees for honey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Empty, vacant, void, devoid, or unoccupied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a place, thing, or vessel that contains no occupants or contents.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Free, clear, or quit of a thing, person, affair, or anxiety.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with مِنْ or عَنْ and may describe freedom from worry, liability, an affliction, or another matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Without a wife; of a woman, without a husband, and in some uses without husband or children.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival social-status use, with feminine and plural forms reported in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Alone or by oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A contextual adjectival use of being in a vacant place or without companions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Destitute of or lacking something, including additional wives in the reported idiom.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited phrase explicitly concerns not finding a man without wives besides the speaker; it is not simply the feminine marital-status adjective خَلِيَّةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel left alone and separated from her young one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Left free, permitted, or allowed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive participle of Form II; it describes someone or something released from restraint or permission being granted.
